entries.title: Mathematical Principles and Experimental Discoveries of the Emergence of Symbolic Patterns in Artificial Neural Networks
entries.summary: Claims that ANN inference logic can be reformulated as sparse symbolic interactions and proves two implicit mathematical criteria that force such emergence, with empirical transferability across samples and models.
entries.takeaway: Under two implicit criteria satisfied by most inputs, ANN inference reduces to a sparse symbolic-interaction representation that transfers across samples and models.

lessons.point: The claim is architecture-agnostic: the emergence proof does not depend on a specific ANN architecture.
lessons.excerpt: the observed emergence of symbolic patterns in ANNs suggests that similar symbolic representations may also emerge in other types of black-box systems under certain conditions, because our proof does not depend on any specific ANN architecture.

lessons.point: Two mathematical criteria are proven sufficient for sparse symbolic interactions to emerge.
lessons.excerpt: We further prove that two common mathematical criteria, which are implicitly required across tasks, lead to the emergence of such sparse symbolic interactions.

lessons.point: Interactions transfer sample-to-sample and model-to-model, evidencing faithfulness rather than post-hoc curve-fitting.

entries.title: Multi-Legal-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Legal Reasoning Across Jurisdictions, Languages, and Legal Traditions
entries.summary: Cross-jurisdictional legal-NLP benchmark with identical tasks across six European countries and 165M full-text court decisions. Evaluates 7 frontier LLMs zero-shot and 3-shot via Bedrock plus 4 small/medium models. Key findings: no single model dominates any language, cross-lingual few-shot transfer is predicted by label-set alignment rather than language family, and tokenizer fertility does not predict cross-lingual accuracy.
entries.takeaway: Legal-domain multilingual benchmark. The methodological finding — label-set alignment beats language proximity for cross-lingual transfer — is the only durable takeaway; the rest is domain-specific.

lessons.point: Cross-lingual few-shot transfer between LLMs is predicted by how well label sets align across languages, not by language-family proximity.
lessons.excerpt: cross-lingual few-shot transfer does not follow language proximity: UA->FR (Romance, -2.0 pp) transfers better than UA->PL (Slavic, -13.8 pp), with label-set alignment predicting transfer quality better than language family

lessons.point: Tokenizer fertility (a common efficiency proxy across languages) does not significantly predict cross-lingual accuracy despite a 2.3x spread across languages; architecture and pretraining data dominate.
lessons.excerpt: tokenizer fertility, despite a 2.3x spread, does not significantly predict cross-lingual accuracy (r=-0.14, p=0.24), suggesting that model architecture and pretraining data dominate tokenizer efficiency.

entries.title: Recovering Lesion Parameters from Aphasic Picture Naming Error Profiles in Large Language Models
entries.summary: Trains inverse models on 4,840 lesion configurations of LLaVA-Vicuna 13B to recover perturbation parameters from picture-naming error profiles. Modification percentage and noise sigma are recoverable; layer index is only recoverable within a neighborhood, yet counterfactual perturbation reproduces target behavior in 81.4% of cases — consistent with functional redundancy across transformer layers.
entries.takeaway: Behavior-to-parameter inverse mapping in LLMs shows that some perturbation parameters are recoverable while layer index is not, evidence of functional redundancy across transformer layers that standard interpretability misses.

lessons.point: Interpretability methods describe internal state but do not test causal sufficiency; counterfactual validation does.
lessons.excerpt: Interpretability methods for large language models (LLMs) describe internal state but do not directly test whether that state is causally sufficient to produce the observed behavior.

lessons.point: Layer index is only recoverable within a neighborhood despite high counterfactual fidelity.
lessons.excerpt: modification percentage and noise sigma were recoverable, whereas layer index was recoverable only within a neighborhood.

lessons.point: Dissociation between low layer recovery and high counterfactual fidelity implies functional redundancy across transformer layers.
lessons.excerpt: This dissociation between low layer recovery and high counterfactual fidelity is consistent with functional redundancy across transformer layers, a property not captured by standard interpretability methods.

actionable.title: Track counterfactual validation as an interpretability standard
actionable.detail: For any interpretability claim about which layer or component produces which behavior, functional redundancy means single-layer attributions are likely under-identified; require counterfactual reproduction, not just correlation with internal state.

entries.title: RoRA: Role-Oriented Regional Allocation for Visual Token Pruning in MLLMs
entries.summary: Training-free visual-token pruning for MLLMs (LLaVA, Qwen-VL) that partitions image tokens into a protected semantic core, complementary context, and fine detail; reports 96.5% of full performance at 88.9% pruning and 1.33x end-to-end speedup at 66.7% pruning on H800. It's an inference-efficiency paper adjacent to cluster C (Model I/O and tokens) but with no security threat model, no adversarial pruning analysis, and no attacker-controlled input framing.
entries.takeaway: Notable inference-efficiency result for MLLMs (Pareto-good visual-token pruning), but nothing security-relevant.

lessons.point: Framing pruning as region-level evidence allocation with explicit roles for retained tokens differentiates this method from importance/diversity/coverage baselines.
lessons.excerpt: We present RoRA, a training-free framework that casts visual token pruning as role-oriented regional evidence allocation. Given a fixed budget, RoRA partitions tokens into a protected semantic core, complementary context, and fine-grained detail.

lessons.point: Attention-Anchored Regions built from high-confidence anchors serve as proxies for which object support is already covered, avoiding wasted retention.
lessons.excerpt: It first calibrates text-conditioned attention with a positional prior and a prompt-calibrated object prior, then builds Attention-Anchored Regions (AARs) from high-confidence anchors as lightweight proxies for covered object support.

lessons.point: Efficiency numbers are concrete and workload-shaped: sub-millisecond selection overhead with a measurable end-to-end speedup.
lessons.excerpt: At a 66.7% pruning ratio, RoRA requires only 0.7 ms for token selection and reduces end-to-end inference time by 24.6%, corresponding to a 1.33x speedup over unpruned inference on an NVIDIA H800.

entries.title: Scalable Long-Horizon Planning with Staggered Updates for Lifelong MAPF

It claims to coordinate 10,000 agents in under a second while beating baselines on system throughput across two realistic MAPF scenarios. The subject is physical/robot fleet coordination, not LLM-agent orchestration, so this lands in the news-adjacent lane rather than the harness/claims track.

lessons.point: Staggered planning windows let a subset of agents replan per timestep, reducing per-tick planning cost without giving up multi-step horizon reasoning.
lessons.excerpt: Like TP, PUSH reduces computational complexity by planning only a subset of agents at each timestep using staggered planning windows. Unlike TP, however, PUSH plans RHCR-style windowed paths in general maps without relying on restrictive map assumptions.

entries.title: Shaping Human-AI Interactions to Provide Improvement Pathways and Balance Competing Objectives
entries.summary: Thesis studying human-AI interaction loops where individuals form beliefs about a deployed AI and strategically present themselves to secure favorable outcomes. Aims to design interactions that help users form accurate beliefs at minimal cost, encourage genuine improvement over gaming, and preserve the AI system's stated objectives. Integrates theory, data-driven modeling, human-subject experiments, and empirical evaluations.
entries.takeaway: When a deployed AI evaluates people, interaction design should treat strategic self-presentation as a first-class dynamic to be shaped, not a nuisance to be filtered.

lessons.point: Deployed AI systems produce interaction loops where evaluated individuals strategically shape their inputs to fit their model of the system.
lessons.excerpt: When an AI system is deployed, the individuals who use and or are evaluated by it form beliefs about how the system operates and use those beliefs to strategically present their preferences, behaviors, or attributes.

lessons.point: The stated design goals are accurate user beliefs at low cost, encouraging improvement over gaming, and preserving system objectives like accuracy.
lessons.excerpt: (1) help individuals develop accurate beliefs about the AI systems so they can improve and or secure favorable outcomes at minimal cost, (2) encourage improvement and or discourage gaming behaviors, and (3) ensure that the AI system continues to achieve its intended objectives, such as maximizing accuracy.

actionable.title: Frame gaming resistance as an interaction-design objective, not a filter
actionable.detail: If deploying an AI that scores or evaluates users, include strategic-behavior response as an explicit design target alongside accuracy, and separate 'genuine improvement' from 'gaming' in your metrics rather than treating both as noise.

entries.title: Stochastic Autoregressive Learning
entries.summary: PAC-style learning-theory model for binary stochastic autoregressive generators. Compares sample complexity of learning from base one-step samples, chain-of-thought trajectories, and end-to-end final-token samples; shows no universal ordering at fixed error scale, but scale-adjusted upper bounds relate the three regimes.
entries.takeaway: Stochastic autoregressive learning is not a straight extension of the deterministic theory: CoT vs base vs end-to-end sample complexity cannot be universally ordered at fixed scale, only after re-scaling.

lessons.point: The stochastic setting fundamentally differs from the deterministic autoregressive-learning theory it generalizes.
lessons.excerpt: We show that stochastic autoregressive learning fundamentally differs from the deterministic theory.

lessons.point: At fixed error scale, sample-complexity ratios between CoT/base and e2e/CoT can be made arbitrarily large.
lessons.excerpt: At scale ε, there is no universal comparison between the three learning tasks: both m C o T/m b a s eand m e 2 e/m C o Tcan be made simultaneously arbitrarily larger than M/ε, the natural analogue for the existing deterministic results.

lessons.point: After rescaling, CoT learning at scale ε is upper-bounded by base learning at scale ε/M^2.
lessons.excerpt: for every class, CoT learning at scale εis upper-bounded by base learning at scale ε/M 2, whereas e2e learning at scale εis upper-bounded, up to logarithmic factors, by (M/ε)m C o T(Θ(ε)).

entries.title: An AI4AI Framework for Visual Token Pruning
entries.summary: AutoPrune has an LLM design visual-token pruning policies for multimodal LLMs via a Token Pruning DSL (131 atoms) that expresses each candidate policy as a residual modification of a strong base policy. Reports 94.4% token removal while preserving >99% of full-token performance, 9.9x FLOPs reduction, and 6.4x prefill-latency reduction.
entries.takeaway: Framing algorithm design as residual edits over a strong base policy, in a task-specific DSL, is the load-bearing trick that lets an LLM's general reasoning translate into competitive pruning policies.

lessons.point: The DSL's key trick is representing each search state as a residual on a strong base policy, narrowing the search space.
lessons.excerpt: A key property of TPDSL is that it represents each search state as a residual modification of a strong base policy. This residual formulation narrows the search space and directs the LLM's attention toward the policy components that are most consequential for performance.

lessons.point: Effective LLM-as-designer requires a search-state representation that bridges general LLM knowledge and task structure.
lessons.excerpt: We argue that the key lies in designing an appropriate search-state representation that connects the internal knowledge of LLMs with the structural requirements and constraints of visual-token pruning.

lessons.point: Reported gains: 94.4% visual tokens removed at >99% of full-token performance, 9.9x FLOPs and 6.4x prefill speedup.

entries.title: Capacity Confounds and Coverage Guarantees in Adaptive Sub-model Federated Learning
